MO.name: Missouri
MO.agency: Missouri Department of Social Services (MO HealthNet Division) / Missouri Rural Health Transformation Office — 'ToRCH Care' (Transformation of Rural Community Health Care)
MO.status_note: CMS approved Missouri's $216M Year 1 budget in April 2026. DSS has issued a Vital Rural Hospital Repairs IFB (Apr 2026), selected 27 ToRCH Care Hub Anchors (Jul 2026), signed mobile-health (~$6.5M) and doula-workforce ($733K) partnerships, opened a Smart Growth & Service Line IFB (up to $5M/award) and a Virtual Care Expansion RFI (RPM for maternal care, telehealth specialist access; closed 2026-09-09). Roughly $130M committed by mid-August; Year 1 funds must be obligated by 2026-10-30.

sources.note: Main RHTP/ToRCH Care page: current RFPs/RFIs/IFBs, hub anchor list, webinars, newsletters, GovDelivery bulletins.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.agency: Tennessee Department of Health — 'Rural Health Access for Tennessee's Future' / Tennessee RHTP
TN.status_note: TDH rolled out nine competitive RHTP grant opportunities weekly from 2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10 via its Caspio Partner Portal. On 2026-09-03 it announced the first 53 awards (HART built-environment projects in 44 counties). Awards for the remaining lines are pending; TDH aims to commit all Year 1 funds by the CMS 2026-10-30 deadline.

sources.note: Eight competitive grant lines (Service Line Expansion & Co-Location, Maternal & Child Health, MaRTHA, Rural Non-Emergency Transportation, Health-Tech, CARE, Healthy Built Environment, Policy/Systems/Environmental); reimbursement-based grants; links to Partner Portal.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.agency: Office of the Governor — Mississippi RHTP Office, with the Mississippi State Department of Health and Division of Medicaid
MS.status_note: Mississippi stood up a Governor's-office RHTP Office and MississippiRHTP.com in Apr 2026, opened three provider grant programs (technology, capital care-gap closure, telehealth) in June that drew 724 applications, and on 2026-09-14 announced 167 awards totaling $104.1M. WEI and PES/EmPATH awards expected roughly late Oct 2026; further opportunities for innovative rural care and EHR modernization slated to open in October.

sources.note: Five initiatives: CRIS, WEI, HTAM, TAPS, BRIDGE.

Funding opportunities page: RCGC, RTG, TCE selections complete; WEI and PES-EmPATH (Jul 15 to Aug 17 2026) closed and under review; EMS Capacity Assessment RFP closed 2026-07-24; HIE consultant opportunity via Knowledge Services.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.agency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH) / Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability (ORHTS)
LA.status_note: All seven Year 1 NOFOs closed between 2026-06-25 and 2026-08-14. The Rural Clinician Credit Bank has awarded $12.7M to 53 facilities across 28 parishes; Notices of Intent to Contract for the other six programs were slated for September 2026. Rural Tech Catalyst Fund Cohort 1 awards expected mid-Oct 2026; Year 2 NOFOs (including an EHR voucher NOFO) targeted for ~Nov 2026; next Advisory Council meeting 2026-11-05.

sources.note: Lists all Year 1 NOFOs, monthly webinar slides, surveys (EPIC interest, EHR/interoperability, VBC/APM readiness) and an Important Dates block. Site returns 403 to non-browser user agents; curl with a browser User-Agent.

Seven Year 1 NOFOs (Rural Clinician Credit Bank, Collaborative Provider Models, Rural Medicaid APM, Regional Care Conveners, Food is Medicine, Telehealth Infrastructure, Rural Health Facilities Capital Improvement). Year 1 deadlines Jun 25 to Aug 14 2026; Year 2 windows expected ~Nov 2026.
Rural Tech Catalyst Fund run by LDH + Louisiana Innovation for health-tech startups; Cohort 1 awards expected mid-Oct 2026, Cohort 2 opening soon.
July 2026 RFI for implementation workforce for a state-managed rural EHR (Epic Community Connect model); an EHR Voucher NOFO for providers is planned for grant period 2.
Sept 2026 webinar slides: Rural Clinician Credit Bank results (53 awards, $12.7M) and EHR voucher program design.

TX.name: Texas
TX.agency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), Provider Finance Department — 'Rural Texas Strong'
TX.status_note: CMS approved Rural Texas Strong on 2026-04-07. HHSC opened Initiative 1 (MRTHA direct awards to ~80 rural hospital districts, ~$250M), Initiative 4 (workforce, $99M; rounds due 2026-05-27 and 2026-08-26) and Initiative 6 Part 1 (equipment, $70.4M) in Apr to Jun 2026, with notices of award Jun to Sep 2026 and programs starting 2026-09-30. Initiatives 2 (patient portals/RPM), 3 (AI/telehealth) and 5 (cybersecurity) are scheduled to open Oct to Dec 2026 with awards Jan to Mar 2027. HIGH relevance for Allstar Partners.

sources.note: Full initiative timeline table (application deadlines, notice-of-award and contract dates for Initiatives 1 to 6), project narratives, NOAs, FAQs. Applicants use the HHSC Grants Management System.
HHSC RFA/grants listing (Rural Texas Strong RFAs such as HHS0017212 Initiative 4).
HHSC newsroom (e.g. 2026-04-29 $99M workforce release).
Electronic State Business Daily; HHSC says Rural Texas Strong vendor procurements post here and are announced via GovDelivery topic TXHHSC_1016.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.agency: Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH) lead, with Oklahoma Health Care Authority (OKSHINE HIE), State Dept. of Education and Healthcare Workforce Training Commission
OK.status_note: Funds released to OSDH 2026-03-06; 29 programs launched in Budget Period 1. Microgrants awarded to 73 organizations in 68 of 75 rural counties, 60 ROOTS school grants made, 20 organizations notified of Rural Regional Reorientation awards; Doula, EMS vehicle, Behavioral Health Integration and Chronic Disease Management rounds closed with awardee lists not yet posted. Budget Period 1 funds must be obligated by 2026-10-30; Budget Period 2 opportunities expected Jan 2027.

sources.note: Six initiatives, 32 sub-initiatives; regional champions, roadshows, FAQs, legislative quarterly reports.

Open and closed NOFOs. ROOTS Year 2 school grants open through 2026-10-15; closed: Microgrants, Rural Regional Reorientation, Doulas, EMS/Community Paramedicine vehicles, Behavioral Health Integration, Chronic Disease Management.
